check: the complete workflow for the human visual check
why: Knowing a preview task exists is not the same as knowing what a person has to do. The task launches a client but has no automation arguments, so the steps matter.
workflow: 1. Run gradlew runWallPreview. prepareWallPreview first writes the two marker files and a preview-runtime.json into build/run/wallPreview, then the task starts a real client with -Dgreatwall.s1c.productionFixture=true.
2. The client opens at the main menu. There is no --quickPlaySingleplayer, so a person creates or opens a single-player world by hand.
3. Loading that world starts the integrated server in the same JVM, so it sees the same -D flag, and its game directory is the same path the markers were written into.
4. Server-starting reads productionFixture plus the two markers and authorises the isolated path, at which point generation begins.
whyTheFlagIsNotIgnored: It looks like the client ignores productionFixture because the client source set never reads it. It does not need to: the integrated server shares the JVM, so the system property is visible to it.
markerLocationMatches: Both markers go into build/run/wallPreview, which is also the --gameDir and therefore FabricLoader's game directory for the integrated server.
whatTheHumanSees: A wall generating in front of them, which is the check automation cannot perform.
